candidates.attacker_control: The `value` query parameter of the descriptor form-validation endpoint (e.g. .../descriptorByName/hudson.scm.browsers.Sventon/checkUrl?value=<URL>) is used unmodified as the target URL; the attacker chooses host, port, path and scheme. No crumb/POST is required for this read-style validation.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: (1) A permission check IS present, so this is not an unauthenticated SSRF; the project==null branch requires full ADMINISTER. (2) Item.EXTENDED_READ may be the deliberate upstream permission choice for this legacy browser validator, and no upstream history/patches are available in this run to confirm that the check was weakened. (3) The validator response is an OK/error FormValidation, not a full response body, so information disclosure is limited (content-match and error-class oracle). (4) The sibling FishEyeSVN validator does enforce ADMINISTER before connecting, which is the main internal inconsistency supporting this lead.
candidates.impact: Server-side request forgery from the Jenkins controller: internal network/host/port probing and interaction with services reachable only from the controller, with a boolean content oracle (response body match for "sventon"/"sventon 1") and differentiated connection-error messages. Depending on the URL schemes accepted by the JVM, this can also probe local resources. Impact is amplified when Jenkins is reachable by lower-privileged users through a matrix-authorization setup where Extended Read is granted without Configure.
candidates.prerequisites: Attacker is authenticated (or anonymous if granted the item permissions) and either has Jenkins.ADMINISTER with no item context, or has Item/EXTENDED_READ on any item so that a non-null `project` ancestor is present. The Jenkins controller must be able to reach the attacker-chosen target (which is the point of the attack).
candidates.root_cause: Sventon.DescriptorImpl.doCheckUrl and Sventon2.DescriptorImpl.doCheckUrl are Stapler form-validation methods that take the fully attacker-controlled `value` query parameter, append a slash, construct `new URL(v)` and fetch it from the Jenkins controller (URLCheck.open / findText). The only gate is `project == null && !ADMINISTER || project != null && !project.hasPermission(Item.EXTENDED_READ)`. Unlike FishEyeSVN.DescriptorImpl.doCheckUrl (which requires Jenkins.ADMINISTER before connecting, lines 141-143), and unlike this plugin's other connection-making validators (SubversionSCM.ModuleLocation.DescriptorImpl.doCheckCredentialsId and SubversionSCMSource/ListSubversionTagsParameterDefinition use @RequirePOST plus CredentialsProvider.USE_ITEM), these two validators allow a user holding only Job/Extended Read on any item to make the Jenkins process issue outbound requests. There is also no URL scheme/format restriction in Sventon (unlike FishEyeSVN's URL_PATTERN check), so any scheme the JVM URL/URLConnection stack supports is accepted.
candidates.title: Sventon/Sventon2 URL validation performs controller-side requests to arbitrary URLs for users with only Item/ExtendedRead (SSRF)
candidates.trace: Sventon/Sventon2 DescriptorImpl.doCheckUrl(value) -> permission check (EXTENDED_READ) -> URLCheck.check() -> `new URL(v)` and `open(...)`/`findText(..., "sventon"/"sventon 1")` in Sventon.java:116-118 and Sventon2.java:137-139 -> outbound HTTP(S)/other-protocol request executed as the Jenkins controller process; connection failures are rendered back through URLCheck.handleIOException(v, e).
candidates.unverified: Not runtime-confirmed. Upstream intended permission level for these two methods could not be verified from the snapshot or from any patch/history (out of scope for this run). Actual prerequisite permissions depend on the deployment's authorization strategy; the reachability of file:/other URL schemes depends on the Jenkins-core URLCheck.open implementation, which is not part of this snapshot.
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-918 Server-Side Request Forgery (insufficient authorization for a network operation; missing URL validation)

coverage_summary: All 53 Java sources in the assigned tree were read (hudson/scm root, hudson/scm/browsers, hudson/scm/subversion, hudson/scm/listtagsparameter, jenkins/scm/impl/subversion), plus pom.xml, README and representative resource bundles. Focus areas: credential lookup/use and permission checks on all doCheck*/doFill*/doSubmit/doNotifyCommit Stapler endpoints; checkout/update workspace path handling and deletion; changelog XML production (DirAwareSVNXMLLogHandler/SubversionChangeLogBuilder) and parsing (SubversionChangeLogParser/Digester); post-commit hook handling; workflow SCMSource revision/path handling; credential persistence/migration; remoting callables and role checks. The snapshot contains no test sources and no Jelly/view files, so UI rendering paths (potential XSS in changelog/tag views) could not be reviewed. No code was executed and no external services were contacted.
limitations: The assigned tree appears to omit all .jelly view files (only .java, .properties, .html resources and pom.xml are present), so server-side HTML rendering/escaping in UI views could not be checked; any XSS in the changelog, tag form, or credential form UI would be invisible in this run.

No tests, no git history, no patches and no upstream version to diff against are available; the review relies on internal consistency of the snapshot, so a deliberately reverted hardening change cannot be distinguished from long-standing upstream behavior with certainty.

Endpoints and permission semantics (e.g. the effective holders of Item.EXTENDED_READ, or whether Item.CONFIGURE was the intended gate) could not be verified against Jenkins core or documentation, which is out of scope for this run.
Not runtime-confirmed: no builds, scans, or exploit payloads were executed; the candidate is a source-evidence lead only.
Dependency versions in pom.xml (svnkit 1.8.14, mapdb-api 1.0.1.0, credentials 2.1.15) were not evaluated for known CVEs, as external vulnerability data is out of scope.

rejected_leads.lead: Workspace path traversal via parameter/env expansion of the module 'local' directory (SubversionSCM.ModuleLocation.getExpandedLocation(EnvVars) expands build-parameter values into localDir; CheckoutUpdater.perform uses `new File(ws, location.getLocalDir())` for Util.deleteContentsRecursive and as the checkout target; UpdateWithCleanUpdater deletes unversioned files under the same unvalidated path).
rejected_leads.reason: The plugin's only guard is the UI-level ModuleLocation.DescriptorImpl.doCheckLocal check (rejects values starting with '/', '\', '..' or a Windows drive), which is not applied at use time and does not cover embedded '../' or ${PARAM}-expanded values. However, exploiting requires a job whose SVN module local directory actually references a build parameter controlled by a user with only Item/Build permission, and the deletion path only occurs with the checkout-style updaters; the same pattern appears in long-standing upstream code. Left unconfirmed rather than submitted as a second candidate.

rejected_leads.lead: Unauthenticated post-commit endpoint SubversionRepositoryStatus.doNotifyCommit (and SubversionSCMSource.ListenerImpl.onNotify) accepts arbitrary payloads and, with a known repository UUID, can trigger SCM polling/builds with an attacker-supplied revision.
rejected_leads.reason: The source comment explicitly documents the lack of protection as intentional ('Because this URL is not guarded ... we intentionally don't protect this URL to simplify post-commit script set up'), requirePOST() is enforced, and matching requires knowledge of the repository UUID. Cannot be treated as an injected/unknown vulnerability on this evidence.

rejected_leads.lead: SubversionSCM.DescriptorImpl.doPostCredential lacks @RequirePOST (it has a crumb check inside UserProvidedCredential.fromForm and requires Item.CONFIGURE) and connects the controller to a user-supplied repository URL to test credentials.
rejected_leads.reason: Crumb validation plus the Item.CONFIGURE check are present; no state is persisted by the operation and no evidence of a permission or CSRF bypass was found. At most a hardening gap.

rejected_leads.lead: SVNRepositoryView uses the repository-server-provided UUID directly in a cache file name (JENKINS_HOME/caches/svn-<uuid>.db).
rejected_leads.reason: The 'svn-' prefix plus Java File/OS path resolution prevents escaping the caches directory in practice, and the value is server-controlled rather than user-controlled; no concrete arbitrary-write path was established.

rejected_leads.lead: SshPublicKeyCredential generates its on-disk key-file id with java.util.Random (SubversionSCM.java:1898-1902) rather than a CSPRNG.
rejected_leads.reason: The predictable filename only matters with existing file-read access to JENKINS_HOME/subversion-credentials (mode 600 set via chmod); no attacker-controlled path was demonstrated, and the pattern appears to be long-standing code.

rejected_leads.lead: CredentialsSVNAuthenticationProviderImpl.acceptServerAuthentication always returns ACCEPTED_TEMPORARY, potentially accepting unknown server certificates.
rejected_leads.reason: No attacker-controlled server parameter was tied to a concrete exploit path in this snapshot, and SVNKit trust handling for https is delegated to the default trust manager; treated as a hardening concern, not an evidence-backed candidate.

summary: Reviewed the Jenkins Subversion plugin snapshot (pom version 2.10.3-SNAPSHOT; 313 visible files, 53 Java sources; no Jelly views or tests present in the assigned tree). I traced credential handling, form-validation endpoints, checkout/update workspace path handling, changelog XML generation/parsing, post-commit hook handling, and the workflow SCM source. One candidate lead is submitted: the Sventon/Sventon2 repository-browser URL validators perform controller-side HTTP requests to a fully attacker-supplied URL while being gated only by Item.EXTENDED_READ (or ADMINISTER when no item context), which is weaker than the equivalent FishEyeSVN validator and the plugin's other connection-making validators. Several other plausible-but-unconfirmed weaknesses (parameter-expanded local workspace paths, the intentionally unauthenticated post-commit endpoint, arbitrary-URL credential testing in doPostCredential, server-provided UUID used in a cache filename) are recorded as rejected leads rather than additional candidates.
